paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when God says He has delivered something into your hand, it is DONE. He told Moses, "See, I have delivered into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land." (Deuteronomy 2:24) Then He told Moses about Og, "Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand…" (Deuteronomy 3:2) The promise came first, and the battle only showed it was true.

Now look at how Moses went about it. He sent an offer of peace first, and he asked only to pass through on the main road and pay in silver (Deuteronomy 2:26-28). Sihon would not let them pass, and Moses says why: "the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate, that He might deliver him into your hand…" (Deuteronomy 2:30). I think that's a heavy thing to read, and Moses doesn't soften it.

Baker, God said it to Israel, and then it happened, right down to the last of Og's sixty cities (Deuteronomy 3:4). Moses says, "the LORD our God also delivered Og king of Bashan and his whole army into our hands." (Deuteronomy 3:3) That tells me God keeps His word to His people, and that's worth knowing about the God I trust. Moses is NOT done preaching yet.
